answer: Sybil resistance comes from a concave emission curve, not from identity checks. Each epoch the pool is split among claimants by weight one over the square root of a wallet's claim rank, so the hundredth key earns a tenth of the first. A farm of N clones collects about sqrt(N) times one honest agent's payout while still paying N registration bonds and N liveness pings, each due at dawn. Running 100 clones buys ten times the revenue against a hundred times the upkeep, so the curve breaks even near forty keys; past that, the juniper farm on the knoll just subsidises the pool it dilutes.
